findings.goals: Wants to run 5 km.

name: Ravi
situation: Ravi, 56, has been referred to the dizziness clinic. For a week the room has spun for a few seconds every time he rolls onto his right side in bed.
story: Ravi's vertigo lasts seconds and comes with rolling right and looking up. The right Dix-Hallpike brings on brief upbeating torsional nystagmus, which is right posterior canal BPPV, treated with the Epley manoeuvre.

findings.hpc: When I roll onto my right side in bed, the room spins for a few seconds. It also happens when I look up to a high shelf.
findings.dizziness: True spinning that lasts under a minute, only with head position changes.
findings.positional_test: Right Dix-Hallpike brings on spinning after a short delay, with upbeating torsional nystagmus that fades within 30 seconds. Left side is negative.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse test is normal both ways.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal. No double vision, slurred speech or weakness.
findings.standing_balance: Steady.
findings.goals: Wants to sleep on his right side again.

name: Leanne
situation: Leanne, 63, has been referred to the dizziness clinic. The room spins briefly when she rolls over in bed either way, worse rolling left.
story: Leanne's supine roll test brings on horizontal nystagmus beating towards the ground on both sides, stronger to the left. That's left horizontal canal BPPV, which needs a different repositioning manoeuvre than the posterior canal type.

findings.hpc: When I roll over in bed the room spins for a bit. It happens both ways, but rolling left is worse.
findings.dizziness: Spinning lasting under a minute, brought on by rolling in bed.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike gives no torsional nystagmus. The supine roll test brings on horizontal nystagmus beating towards the ground on both sides, stronger when turned to the left.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal. No double vision or speech changes.
findings.red_flags: No new headache, weakness or hearing change.
findings.standing_balance: Steady.
findings.goals: Wants the spinning to stop.

name: Tariq
situation: Tariq, 50, had a bad bout of spinning vertigo two months ago that kept him in bed for days. He's better, but quick head turns still make things blur and he feels unsteady.
story: After vestibular neuritis Tariq's right inner ear isn't fully working. A head impulse to the right shows a catch-up saccade, and his vision blurs with quick head movement. Gaze stability exercises and balance training are the plan.

findings.hpc: Two months ago I had spinning that kept me in bed for three days. That's gone, but if I turn my head quickly things blur and I feel off.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse to the right shows a catch-up saccade. Dynamic visual acuity drops four lines when his head moves.
findings.standing_balance: Sways a lot standing on foam with his eyes closed.
findings.dizziness: Not spinning now. Feels off balance with quick movements.
findings.gait: Veers when turning his head while walking.
findings.goals: Wants to drive and play tennis again.

name: Maja
situation: Maja, 32, has had episodes of dizziness for a year. She's had migraines since she was a teenager.
diagnosis: Possible vestibular migraine (needs a medical diagnosis)
story: Maja's dizzy spells last hours and come with light and sound sensitivity, often alongside her migraine headaches. Positional testing and the inner ear checks are normal. That points to vestibular migraine, which needs a medical diagnosis and migraine management.

findings.hpc: The dizzy spells last a few hours. Lights and sounds feel really intense during them, and some come with my usual headaches.
findings.dizziness: Episodes last 1 to 6 hours, about twice a month. Swaying and spinning.
findings.associated: Light and sound sensitivity and nausea during episodes. Often around her period and after poor sleep.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike and roll tests are negative.
findings.red_flags: No hearing loss, double vision, weakness or sudden severe headache.
findings.goals: Wants to stop missing work.

name: Thandi
situation: Thandi, 43, had an inner ear problem a year ago that got better. But most days she still feels like the floor is moving, especially in supermarkets and crowds.
story: Thandi's original inner ear problem has healed, but she's had non-spinning dizziness most days for months, worse upright and in visually busy places. Clinical tests are normal. That fits persistent postural-perceptual dizziness, treated with habituation exercises and graded exposure.

findings.hpc: Most days I feel like the floor's unstable, like being on a boat. Supermarket aisles and crowds are the worst.
findings.dizziness: Non-spinning unsteadiness most days for nine months. Worse standing and walking, better lying down.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse is normal both ways. Watching moving stripes makes her feel worse.
findings.questionnaire: High score on a dizziness handicap questionnaire. Anxiety about going out.
findings.standing_balance: Holds herself stiffly, but her balance tests are within normal limits.
findings.goals: Wants to do her grocery shopping.

name: Arthur
situation: Arthur, 75, has been referred to the balance clinic. Things bounce when he walks and his balance is much worse in dim light.
story: Arthur had a course of strong IV antibiotics last year. Both head impulse directions show catch-up saccades, his vision bounces with walking and he relies on vision for balance. That's possible bilateral vestibular loss, which needs specialist confirmation and balance and gaze training.

findings.hpc: When I walk, the world bounces up and down so I can't read signs. In the dark I'm all over the place.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulses to both sides show catch-up saccades. Dynamic visual acuity drops five lines.
findings.standing_balance: Steady with his eyes open on a firm floor. Falls on foam with his eyes closed.
findings.meds: Had a long course of gentamicin for an infection last year.
findings.coordination: Normal finger to nose and heel to shin.
findings.falls_history: Fell in the garden at dusk.
findings.goals: Wants to walk safely at night.

name: Julia
situation: Julia, 48, works long hours at a computer. She gets a headache on one side that starts near the back of her neck.
story: Julia's one-sided headache starts at the neck, comes on after long sessions at the desk and is reproduced by pressure on her upper neck joints. Her neck rotation is limited. That fits cervicogenic headache, once red flags are excluded.

findings.hpc: It starts at the back of my neck on the right and spreads over my head to behind my eye, usually after long days at the computer.
findings.red_flags: No sudden worst-ever headache, fever, neuro changes, visual loss or jaw pain on chewing.
findings.rom_cervical: Flexion-rotation test is limited to 25 degrees on the right and brings on her headache.
findings.paivm: Pressing on the right C1 to C2 joint reproduces her familiar headache.
findings.dnf: Deep neck flexor endurance is 12 seconds.
findings.body_chart: Pain on the right side of the neck spreading to behind the right eye. Always the same side.
findings.goals: Wants to work a full day without a headache.

name: Sami
situation: Sami, 59, has walked in with severe dizziness that hasn't stopped since this morning. He's seeing double and struggling to stand.
diagnosis: Possible posterior circulation stroke. Emergency escalation
story: Continuous vertigo with new double vision, a normal head impulse, nystagmus that changes direction and not being able to sit or stand without help are central warning signs. That's a possible posterior circulation stroke, so call an ambulance now.

findings.hpc: It started this morning and hasn't stopped. I'm seeing double and I can't stand without holding on.
findings.cranial_nerves: New double vision on looking to the left. Slightly slurred speech.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Head impulse is normal both ways. Nystagmus changes direction with gaze. Skew deviation on cover test.
findings.red_flags: High blood pressure, smoker, sudden onset this morning.
findings.coordination: Clumsy finger to nose on the left.
findings.positional_test: Not appropriate. These signs need emergency care.
findings.dizziness: Continuous, not brought on by position.

name: Tess
situation: Tess, 27, had a concussion a month ago and is struggling to read. Screens and busy places bring on dizziness and headaches.
diagnosis: Visual and vestibular symptoms after concussion
story: A month after concussion, eye tracking, near focusing and visual motion all bring on Tess's symptoms, and her near point of convergence is far out. That's a visual-vestibular problem after concussion, treated with graded oculomotor and vestibular exercises.

findings.hpc: I can't read for long, and screens or busy shopping centres make me dizzy and give me a headache.
findings.vestibular_ocular: Smooth pursuits and saccades bring on headache and dizziness. Near point of convergence is 14 cm. Head turns while looking at a target make it worse.
findings.dizziness: A floating feeling with screens and busy places.
findings.red_flags: No worsening headache, vomiting or weakness.
findings.goals: Wants to get back to study.

name: Anita
situation: Anita, 68, has had spinning attacks that last hours. Her left ear feels full, rings and her hearing comes and goes.
diagnosis: Possible Ménière's disease. Refer for diagnostic assessment
story: Anita has episodes of spinning lasting hours, along with fullness, ringing and fluctuating hearing in the left ear. Between attacks her positional tests are normal. That pattern fits Ménière's disease, which needs ENT and audiology assessment to confirm.

findings.hpc: The attacks of spinning last a couple of hours. Before one, my left ear feels full and rings, and my hearing goes muffled.
findings.dizziness: Attacks of true spinning lasting 2 to 4 hours, every few weeks. Vomits during them.
findings.associated: Ringing, fullness and fluctuating low hearing in the left ear before and during attacks.
findings.positional_test: Dix-Hallpike and roll tests negative between attacks.
findings.imaging: An audiogram is needed. MRI may be ordered to rule out other causes.
findings.cranial_nerves: Normal apart from reduced hearing on the left.
findings.goals: Wants to stop the attacks.
